title: Loading past the elastic limit and unloading
caption: Up to the elastic limit (here 110 MPa at 0.1% strain; illustrative values) the line has gradient E. Past it the wire deforms plastically. Unloading from 250 MPa follows a line parallel to the original one, so stress reaches zero at a permanent strain of 0.37%.
alt: Stress–strain graph: a steep straight line to the elastic limit, a flatter curve beyond it, and an unloading line parallel to the first that meets the strain axis at a permanent strain of 0.37 percent.
description: The horizontal axis is strain in %; the vertical axis is stress in MPa. The values are illustrative.
Loading: σ = Eε with gradient 1100 MPa per % strain (E = 110 GPa) up to the elastic limit at (0.1%, 110 MPa).
Plastic region: the curve flattens as dislocations move, up to (0.6%, 250 MPa) where the load is removed.
Unloading: a line with the same gradient 1100, reaching zero stress at 0.37% strain. That offset is the permanent plastic strain.
